server.maintainedFrom: the Maintenance and Release Schedule of nextcloud/server

tools.label: ESLint
tools.why: nothing checks the frontend sources, so a wrong import is found by the build or not at all
tools.legacyWhy: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8

tools.label: Stylelint
tools.why: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly

tools.label: Psalm
tools.why: the PHP side has no static analysis, which is what catches a wrong type before the server does

tools.label: PHPUnit
tools.why: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change

tools.label: PHP-CS-Fixer
tools.why: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command

tools.label: REUSE
tools.why: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for

tools.label: EditorConfig
tools.why: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does

lines: appinfo/info.xml states no <repository>.
<repository> is the only machine-readable link from a published release back to the source it was built from. Without it nothing that reads the release can tell where its source is.
<website> is not set either.
A link of appinfo/info.xml leads nowhere:
<bugs> https://framagit.org/framasoft/framaspace/custom-apps/nextcloud-vue3-template/-/issues: HTTP 404
The App Store page shows these links as they are; a reader who follows one ends on an error page.
composer.json scripts cs:check, cs:fix call php-cs-fixer, and no PHP-CS-Fixer configuration is in the checkout.
php-cs-fixer fix --dry-run --diff
The command is there to be run, so whoever runs it gets a tool that has nothing to go by - and CI, if it runs the script, reports the failure as the change under test.
The app id is framaspace, the checkout directory is Template-App-Nextcloud-With-VueJS3.

The server finds an app by its directory name, so the installed directory has to be named after the id. A checkout can be named anything, which is why this is a note and not a defect - but a tarball built from this directory name would not load.
Declares Nextcloud 31 to 33; the oldest maintained major is 33 (the Maintenance and Release Schedule of nextcloud/server), the newest released 35 (the release tags of nextcloud/server).
min-version 31 reaches below the oldest maintained major (33), which means the code has to keep working with APIs that are no longer tested upstream.
PHP floor stated once: composer.json requires php ^8.2; appinfo/info.xml declares no php dependency.
Nothing contradicts anything here. Stating it in both places is what keeps a composer install from resolving packages for a PHP the server will not run.
Node stated as ^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0 (package.json engines.node).
Not stated in .nvmrc, so nothing keeps the other places from drifting away from it.
Tooling in the checkout: Psalm (psalm.xml).
No ESLint configuration: nothing checks the frontend sources, so a wrong import is found by the build or not at all.
No Stylelint configuration: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly.
No PHPUnit configuration: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change.
No PHP-CS-Fixer configuration: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command.
No REUSE configuration: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for.
No EditorConfig configuration: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does.
package.json declares the script lint, which no installed workflow runs.
The template lint-eslint of nextcloud/.github runs lint: make workflows-install W=lint-eslint
A check that no workflow runs on a pull request catches only what the contributor who remembers to run it catches.
4 declared packages are named nowhere in the checkout: @nextcloud/vue, linkifyjs, vue-material-design-icons, @vue/tsconfig.

Searched as literal names over 31 files, package.json excluded apart from its non-dependency fields, lockfiles excluded; then as an ESLint shorthand, as what TypeScript takes from a tsconfig, and as a peer of an installed package in package-lock.json. A package loaded some other way is not named anywhere either, so this is a list to check, not a list to remove.
Licence agpl (appinfo/info.xml), AGPL-3.0-or-later (composer.json).
agpl in appinfo/info.xml is a deprecated App Store value, shown there as AGPLv3+, which is AGPL-3.0-or-later. With min-version 31 info.xml can state an SPDX id instead.
No LICENSES/ directory, so the licence text itself is not in the checkout, which is what REUSE and the distributions check for.
Version 1.0.0 in appinfo/info.xml, package.json and package-lock.json.
package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) in the checkout.
The ncmake bootstrap stub is in place (21 lines).
Every directory the shipped PHP reaches through __DIR__ and the frontend through linkTo is in the shipped file set.
